cited_details.statement: A 2022 study constructed a corpus of 2,540 stopping, backing, final consonant deletion process (FCDP), and affrication samples collected from 90 children aged 3–6 years, with each recording annotated by two speech–language pathologists [SOURCE 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9324778/).

The system used three deep-learning classifiers to distinguish the four Chinese SSD subtypes, illustrating how convolutional and recurrent architectures can operationalize expert SLP annotations at scale [SOURCE 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9324778/).

Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT) systems aim to help children learn correct word pronunciations, but the field has lacked consensus among speech-language therapists regarding which systems provide reliable feedback [SOURCE 4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5884147/).

A 2017 study proposed two new GOP techniques for children with SSDs and reported that pronunciation models incorporating explicit knowledge of error patterns yield more accurate phoneme-level classification than a baseline state-of-the-art GOP approach [SOURCE 4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5884147/).

Earlier work similarly leveraged automatic speech recognition technology to facilitate learning of spoken language and reading skills, laying the groundwork for modern CAPT [SOURCE 3](https://aclanthology.org/W12-5808.pdf).
Dysarthria, caused by impaired articulatory control and muscle weakness, produces abnormal speech rate, pitch, and phoneme articulation [SOURCE 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.04337v2).

Automating dysarthria assessment offers a path to low-cost, objective tools that overcome the subjectivity of manual evaluation, but the small size of dysarthria datasets has historically limited model development [SOURCE 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.04337v2).

Self-supervised learning (SSL) representations pre-trained on large unlabeled corpora have recently been shown to enhance automatic speech recognition for dysarthric speech [SOURCE 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.04337v2).

HuBERT emerged as the most versatile feature extractor, achieving accuracy gains of +24.7% in disease classification, +61% in word recognition, and +7.2% in intelligibility classification relative to classical acoustic features [SOURCE 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.04337v2).

A 2015 study introduced an automated tool consisting of a clinician interface, a mobile application, and a speech processing engine to assess productions from children with apraxia of speech [SOURCE 6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167639315000382).

A 2021 longitudinal evaluation of this system examined tablet-based delivery of child speech therapy and reported sustained engagement and measurable gains over time [SOURCE 10](https://psi.engr.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/hair2021taccess.pdf).

Mobile speech therapy applications have been documented to support children with apraxia and other speech disorders by allowing users to select target phonemes and progress through structured levels [SOURCE 8](http://jmr.tums.ac.ir/index.php/jmr/article/download/133/80).

These apps are designed to be usable by parents and individuals without continuous SLP supervision while remaining customizable for professional clinicians, thereby addressing the shortage of intensive therapy opportunities [SOURCE 8](http://jmr.tums.ac.ir/index.php/jmr/article/download/133/80).

First, the small size of pathological speech datasets, particularly for dysarthria and CAS, limits the training of robust end-to-end models; SSL pre-training on large unlabeled corpora is a promising mitigation [SOURCE 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.04337v2).

Second, there remains no consensus among speech-language therapists on which CAPT systems are clinically reliable, and traditional GOP methods are being supplemented or replaced by models that encode explicit error-pattern knowledge [SOURCE 4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5884147/).

Third, the clinical validation of mobile and tablet-based tools requires longitudinal evidence rather than short-term feasibility studies; emerging longitudinal data for CAS therapy apps indicate that sustained engagement is achievable but continued evaluation is needed [SOURCE 10](https://psi.engr.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/hair2021taccess.pdf).

Future systems are likely to integrate SSL-based acoustic representations [SOURCE 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.04337v2), disorder-specific classifiers [SOURCE 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9324778/), and adaptive CAPT feedback [SOURCE 4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5884147/) into unified therapy platforms that span assessment, scoring, and intervention.
